toni: Heads-up: noticed a weird edgecase in the browser SDK when using fetch+streams (not EventSource). On intermittent mobile networks the last chunk sometimes shows up before a middle chunk. No errors or reconnects shown. :confused:
harper: interesting. do you have a minimal repro? are you using ReadableStream and piping to text decoder?
toni: yep, sampleapp uses fetch with `response.body.getReader()` and pushes chunks to onmessage handlers. sometimes order is: 1,4,2,3. small logs:
```
[08:11:01] seq=1 text="Hi"
[08:11:04] seq=4 text="!"
[08:11:08] seq=2 text=", there"
[08:11:09] seq=3 text=" we go"
```
no HTTP status changes.
liyah: could be multiplexing at proxy or a race when the SDK tries to re-open during a slow drain. Do you see overlapping connections (two requests near same time)?
toni: i see a tiny overlap on reconnects in devtools sometimes. also reproduces if i throttle to ~80kbps locally.
harper: serverside possibility: runtime may flush partial buffers in different order when transport frames are split (H2 or TCP). If the client opens a second connection to resume without sync tokens, fragments can interleave. do you have `Last-Event-ID` or a resume token enabled?
toni: we're not using last-event-id. SDK has a resume token feature but off by default.
liyah: short-term mitigation: SDK should buffer on receive and reorder by an explicit `seq` or `id` field if present, or at least expose `emitOutOfOrder` telemetry so customers can see how often this happens. long-term: runtime should add a monotonic seq (either SSE `id:` or header `X-Chunk-Seq`).
harper: also add a small per-chunk session id (`X-Stream-Session`) so clients can dedupe across reconnects. then SDKs can detect duplicates and reorder deterministically.
toni: i'll add a tiny repro to sampleapp (fetch+streams + chromedriver throttle) and a failing unit that simulates proxy splitting frames. anyone know a small tool to force H2 frame splits? nghttp or `h2load` maybe.
liyah: nghttp is our go-to. QA: add a smoke test in sampleapp CI that runs with a local proxy that forces frame splits and low bandwidth so this doesn't regress. also expose `reorderOnSeq:true` in SDK config behind a feature flag so we can A/B it.
harper: nice. also add an observability event when the SDK drops/duplicates/reorders so infra can create an alert when frequency spikes.
devx-bot: created ticket #5199 "browser-sdk(fetch): handle out-of-order chunks for fetch+streams; add reorderOnSeq flag + telemetry" https://git.redwood/infra/issues/5199 :robot_face:
toni: thanks — i'll push the repro and link the issue. will include a tiny test harness and notes for nghttp commands. :thumbsup:
